clue.text: Bid to get cheap-sounding instrument

parts.note: in bridge, to double is a call or bid that raises the stakes

indicators.note: the word for cheap is said out loud to give a different spelling of the same sound

parts.note: something cheap and low is base

explanation.surface: A bidder at auction tries to snap up a bargain musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: '-sounding' turns BASE (cheap, low) into the same-sounding BASS.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest and lowest-pitched bowed string member of the orchestra is a kind of instrument.

clue.text: Busy about article and good book

parts.note: on means concerning or about
the is the definite article
Job is a book of the Bible, the Good Book

explanation.surface: Someone occupied with an essay and a worthy read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a container signal but is ON, as in 'a talk on'.
explanation.definitionFit: On the job is an idiom for at work, busy with a task.

clue.text: Writer's given up where his work goes?

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: An author has quit, and wonders where his work will end up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given up' reads as quitting but means NIB is written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A rejected manuscript proverbially goes into the waste bin.

clue.text: Cut up over court's demand

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means the first piece sits above the next
in a down answer, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to axe is to cut
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A dissected item placed above the court's formal request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns AXE to EXA; 'over' puts it above CT.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to demand and obtain, as in exacting payment.

clue.text: Vessel in which lab mice are sacrificed

indicators.note: creatures sacrificed are destroyed, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A laboratory flask where experimental mice are killed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacrificed' is the anagram signal for LAB MICE; 'in which' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An alembic is an old distilling apparatus, a vessel used by alchemists.

clue.text: A brief shower, that's what we're lacking

parts.note: short means brief
a fall is a shower, as of rain or snow

explanation.surface: A short spell of rain is just what our dry land is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortfall is a deficit, the amount by which supply is lacking.

clue.text: To be very old is a source of distress

explanation.surface: Living to a great age brings its own troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sore' once meant 'very', as in the Bible's 'sore afraid'; 'old' marks that sense as archaic. 'To be' and 'is' just link the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adverb meaning greatly appears in older English, and a painful spot or grievance is a sore point.

clue.text: Money earned by cabbie — that'll turn a few heads

parts.note: screw is old British slang for wages
a cab driver is a cabbie

explanation.surface: A taxi driver's earnings attract plenty of attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn a few heads' suggests attracting stares, but means turning screw heads.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwdriver is the tool for turning the heads of screws.

clue.text: Issue instructions about way to take animals

indicators.note: about means round, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to rule is to direct or issue orders
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: Someone gives directions about a route for driving livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take animals' is the definition: rustling is stealing livestock, not the sound of leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To rustle is to steal cattle or horses.

clue.text: Primitive period's general character comprehended by ancient

indicators.note: to comprehend is to take in or include, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: an ancient is a venerable old man, a sage
the general character or feel of something is its tone

explanation.surface: An essay notes that an ancient writer grasped the spirit of a primitive age.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'period's' is 'is', a link word; 'ancient' is a noun here, a wise old man.
explanation.definitionFit: The earliest era of human prehistory, when tools were made of stone, is the archetypal primitive period.

clue.text: Formidable woman's departure requires new head

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for departure is swapped for another letter

parts.note: an egress is a way out or act of leaving

explanation.surface: A forceful woman's exit calls for a fresh leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requires new head' swaps the first letter, E, of EGRESS for O.
explanation.definitionFit: A female monster from fairy tales is used figuratively of a fearsome, domineering woman.

clue.text: Don't change anything about old way of recording piece by Beethoven

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark meaning let it stand, leave unchanged
an EP, extended play, is an old vinyl record format

explanation.surface: An instruction not to alter an old recording of a Beethoven work.
explanation.walkthrough: STET is the proofreader's 'let it stand', and EP records were a 1950s-80s format.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven wrote a famous Septet in E flat, Op. 20, for seven instruments.

clue.text: Instinctively dislike cooking a giant steak

indicators.note: cooking is preparing, so the words are reworked into a new mix

explanation.surface: Someone has an aversion to preparing a huge steak.
explanation.definitionFit: To take against someone is to develop a dislike for them, often without reason.

clue.text: Royal husband giving good news of newly-delivered wife?

explanation.surface: A royal consort announces that his wife and baby are doing fine.
explanation.walkthrough: James Hepburn, Earl of Bothwell, was the third husband of Mary, Queen of Scots. After a birth, the good news is that mother and baby are both well.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl married Mary Queen of Scots in 1567, and reporting mother and child healthy is the classic happy birth announcement.

clue.text: Causing alarm to head of committee in traditionally peaceful seat

parts.note: rocking can mean shocking or unsettling, as in news rocking a nation
the chair is the person heading a committee

explanation.surface: A committee leader is shaken while sitting somewhere meant to be calm.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat on curved runners that sways gently is the stock image of a calm fireside armchair.

clue.text: Phrase used by foreman when a sentence would be wrong

definitions.text: Phrase used by foreman when a sentence would be wrong

parts.words: Phrase used by foreman when a sentence would be wrong
parts.note: the foreman of a jury announces the verdict that means the accused should not be punished

explanation.surface: A grammar-minded foreman objects to a badly formed sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreman' suggests a factory and 'sentence' grammar, but it is a jury foreman and a court's punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The jury foreman's acquittal verdict means no sentence should be passed.

clue.text: Tone Phil extracted from orchestra

indicators.note: extracted means pulled out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: a philharmonic is a symphony orchestra
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician named Phil pulled out of the orchestra over its sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extracted from' removes PHIL from PHILHARMONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonic is an overtone, a tone above the fundamental pitch.

clue.text: Very old unit alive and kicking

indicators.note: something kicking is moving about lively, so these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: An ancient army unit is still alive and full of fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alive and kicking' looks like a set phrase, but 'kicking' alone is the anagram signal for UNIT ALIVE AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally 'before the Flood', the word is used for anything extremely old or old-fashioned.

clue.text: Like the tills in the customs shed to be working properly?

definitions.text: Like the tills in the customs shed to be working properly?

parts.words: Like the tills in the customs shed to be working properly?
parts.note: read as duty-full, the tills at customs are brimming with import duty

explanation.surface: Customs officers check that their cash registers are functioning.
explanation.walkthrough: The word sounds like 'duty-full', and customs tills fill with duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutiful means conscientious, doing what one ought, as working properly suggests.

clue.text: In shop's promotion, representative piece to try

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a sale is a shop's promotional event
an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: During a store's offer, a free taster is handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: MP stands for Member of Parliament, the UK's elected representative.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample is a small portion offered so one can try it.

clue.text: Weapon from which religious believers receive a light blow

indicators.note: the believers take in the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a cult is a group of religious followers
a tap is a gentle blow

explanation.surface: A sect gets lightly struck by a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light blow' is TAP, not a ray of light; the definition 'Weapon' comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A Y-shaped sling or siege engine for hurling missiles is a weapon.

clue.text: Quiet tear, burying minute little fellow

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: burying means hiding something inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a rip is a tear

explanation.surface: A small man silently weeps over a tiny matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear' reads as weeping but means a rip. 'burying' puts M inside RIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrimp is slang for a very small person, a little man.

clue.text: Has failed to disable old military item

indicators.note: failed means broke down, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: KO, knock out, means to put out of action

explanation.surface: Something has proved unable to put an old army relic out of action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' is the anagram signal for HAS, giving SHA.
explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall peaked cylindrical military hat of the 19th century.

clue.text: Quickly turn left round area, like a column in body

indicators.note: left is brought round to sit after area, so its letter follows

parts.note: to spin is to turn rapidly

explanation.surface: A drill instruction to wheel left around a space, as a column of soldiers might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' sets L after A, giving AL; 'turn left' reads as a drill order but SPIN is all of 'Quickly turn'.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinal column is the backbone, so spinal means relating to that column in the body.

clue.text: Emotional speech on symbol of nationhood is notorious

indicators.note: on means placed after, following the other piece

parts.note: a national flag symbolises a nation
a rant is an impassioned tirade

explanation.surface: A heated speech about the national flag is outrageous.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant means glaringly obvious and shocking, as with a notorious offence.

clue.text: Local prince let drop cry of surprise, given authority in India

indicators.note: let drop means lose, so these letters fall away

parts.note: a rajah is an Indian prince
ah is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A regional prince, startled, lets slip an exclamation under British rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let drop' removes AH from RAJAH; 'given' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Raj was the period of British rule in India, its governing authority.

clue.text: Say imperial units are a remarkable achievement

indicators.note: say signals that the word for the units is spoken, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: feet are imperial units of length

explanation.surface: Using imperial measures nowadays is something of an accomplishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A feat is an impressive deed requiring skill or courage.

clue.text: No plucky sailor gets disease from mosquito

parts.note: not plucky means cowardly, which is yellow
a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A timid sailor catches a tropical illness from a mosquito bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow jack is an old name for yellow fever, a viral disease spread by mosquitoes.
